profile.campus: Manassas, Prince William County, Virginia (QTS Manassas campus)
profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, Manassas DC1 sits at 9400 Godwin Dr, Manassas, VA 20110, part of a planned six-building, 105-acre campus with 190+ MW of critical campus capacity upon completion. This registry carries two separate OSM entries both named QTS Manassas DC1 (this row and osm:way/1134911642), most likely a duplicate map entity; both are documented identically per this project's never-delete/never-merge policy pending manual OSM de-duplication.

QTS Data Centers (shown on this row under its pre-2013-IPO name, "Quality Technology Services") was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas. Per Blackstone's own press release, Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT) and other Blackstone-affiliated funds completed a roughly $10 billion acquisition of QTS Realty Trust on August 31, 2021, taking the company private at $78 per share; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. QTS's own site lists its US headquarters at 22271 Broderick Drive, Sterling, Virginia, placing this Northern Virginia "Data Center Alley" corridor, alongside neighboring hyperscale and colocation campuses from Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, at the center of the company's operations.

Dominion Energy, the dominant electric utility across Northern Virginia's data center corridor, has repeatedly cited data center demand growth as a primary driver of its long-term transmission and generation planning, and Loudoun and Prince William County officials have both cited data center real estate and business-license tax revenue as a significant share of their county budgets. QTS's Virginia campuses sit within this same regional grid and policy environment as neighboring hyperscale and colocation buildings operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, all tracked elsewhere in this registry.

QTS positions itself as a "hyperscale-neutral" wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than operating its own end-user cloud service, a business model shared with peers like Digital Realty and CyrusOne in this same Northern Virginia corridor; under Blackstone ownership since 2021, QTS has continued expanding its US footprint (including its Manassas and Richmond 3 campuses, both still under construction as of the facts recorded here) rather than slowing development after going private.

Northern Virginia is confirmed by Wikipedia as one of QTS's primary operating regions, alongside the separate Richmond, VA campus recorded elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
QTS Manassas DC1 is one building in a planned six-building, 105-acre campus expected to deliver 190+ megawatts of critical capacity upon completion. The campus sits in Prince William County, Virginia, part of the Northern Virginia data center corridor alongside facilities operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, all drawing power from the same regional grid managed by Dominion Energy. At an assumed 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 190 megawatts of IT load would support roughly 4,750 racks of accelerator infrastructure when fully built out.

This campus ranks 24th among the 23 Virginia facilities with published megawatt figures in this registry, though that ranking reflects only the 326 mapped facilities in the state and does not represent Virginia's total data center capacity. The Manassas site is one of three planned Prince William County buildings in QTS's Northern Virginia footprint, alongside DC2 and DC5, and sits within a region where county officials have cited data center real estate and business-license tax revenue as a significant share of their budgets and Dominion Energy has cited data center demand as a primary driver of transmission and generation planning.

QTS operates as a wholesale and colocation landlord, leasing built capacity to enterprise, cloud, and hyperscale tenants rather than running its own cloud service. The company has continued expanding its US footprint under Blackstone ownership since August 2021, including this Manassas campus and a separate Richmond facility, both still under construction as of the published specifications. Specific certifications, current occupancy, tenant identities, and power procurement terms are not published.
